picks.title: Connect v0 apps to Slack, Google, and 100+ other services
picks.excerpt: Apps and agents built in v0 can now securely connect to 100+ third-party services — Slack, Google, Notion, GitHub, Salesforce — through Vercel Connect. Prompt-built prototypes can now reach real company data without a developer wiring the auth.
picks.rationale: Prompt-built prototypes can now hit real company data without a developer wiring auth — it moves the ceiling on what a designer can validate alone.

picks.title: Show Your Work: building motion design plugins for Figma, in Figma
picks.excerpt: A product designer walks through building motion design plugins for Figma himself in Figma's Show Your Work series. The clearest current example of designers shipping their own tooling instead of filing a request.
picks.rationale: A designer building his own motion plugins end to end — the shortest path from 'I wish Figma did X' to actually shipping X.

picks.title: Slack wants to drag AI coding out of the terminal and into the group chat
picks.excerpt: Slack Code embeds coding agents like Claude Code and Devin directly into team channels, turning agent work from a solo terminal session into something a whole team watches, steers and approves. Designers and PMs get a seat at the build loop.
picks.rationale: Agent work moves from a private terminal into the channel — designers can steer and approve builds without ever opening an IDE.

picks.title: Foundry releases Nuke 17.1 with Gaussian splat relighting and Hydra 2.0
picks.excerpt: Foundry's Nuke 17.1 adds relighting for Gaussian splats and Hydra 2.0 support in the 3D viewer. Neural-captured scenes become relightable comp elements, pulling AI-era 3D capture into a standard finishing workflow.
picks.rationale: Relightable Gaussian splats inside Nuke means phone-captured 3D can finally survive a real finishing pipeline instead of staying a demo.

picks.title: Choosing an AI builder: Lovable, Replit, Bolt, Codex or Claude Code
picks.excerpt: A hands-on comparison of Lovable, Replit, Bolt, Codex and Claude Code, matched to the kind of app idea each one actually suits. Practical triage for designers deciding where a prototype should be born.
picks.rationale: Matches each builder to the kind of idea it actually suits — a decision a designer makes before the first prompt, and usually gets wrong.
